short: A hundred and fifty men, a mission station, and eleven Victoria Crosses.
full:
On 22 January 1879, hours after a Zulu army destroyed a British column at Isandlwana, three to four thousand warriors of the uncommitted reserve under Prince Dabulamanzi kaMpande crossed into Natal and attacked the mission station at Rorke's Drift. The garrison numbered about 150, mostly B Company of the 2nd Battalion, 24th Foot, under Lieutenants John Chard and Gonville Bromhead, with some thirty-five men in the hospital.

They built barricades from mealie bags and biscuit boxes and held through the night, losing and burning the hospital, until the Zulus withdrew after dawn on 23 January. Seventeen defenders were killed; Zulu dead ran into the hundreds. Eleven Victoria Crosses were awarded, the most ever for a single action, a decision widely read as an attempt to set something against the disaster at Isandlwana. The Anglo-Zulu War ended in July with the defeat of the Zulu kingdom at Ulundi. Sabaton's "Rorke's Drift", from The Last Stand (2016), is about the night's defence.
